records.summary: 910 Clement St sits in the Inner Clement Street Neighborhood Commercial District where a restaurant serving beer and wine is principally permitted on the first story with no conditional use authorization required. The site history shows continuous restaurant use with Type 41 ABC licenses dating back to at least 2005, most recently as a bakery/limited restaurant approved in 2020. The block is densely saturated with food and beverage operations: 17 registered food/drink businesses within 500 feet, 11 active on-sale ABC licenses within 500 feet (27 within 1,000 feet), and ABC's undue-concentration flag is triggered. The Inner Clement NCD has seen only routine agency referrals approved in recent years; the one dated use decision within 1,000 feet in the last decade was withdrawn.

Site has continuous restaurant use history with Type 41 licenses dating to 2005; most recent approval was a bakery/limited restaurant in October 2020
High density: 17 registered food/drink businesses within 500 feet, including 1 bar (Lost Marbles Brewpub)
Eleven active on-sale ABC licenses within 500 feet, 27 within 1,000 feet; ABC undue-concentration flag triggered
Active Type 41 licenses at immediately adjacent addresses: 908 Clement (issued 2016) and 914 Clement (issued 2016)

comparables.why_comparable: Immediately adjacent address (906 Clement St, next door to 910), Type 41 ABC license for restaurant with full cooking, approved 2016 in the Inner Clement NCD.
comparables.key_takeaway: Type 41 for the restaurant immediately next door (906 Clement) was approved within 28 days as an agency referral. Planning required the operator to 'operate as a Bona Fide Eating Place'—a standard ABC condition—but imposed no other restrictions despite the already dense concentration of licenses on this block.

comparables.why_comparable: 40 meters away at 852 Clement St, Type 41 ABC referral for restaurant, same zoning district (NCD-INNER CLEMENT), decided 2022.
comparables.key_takeaway: Type 41 approved at 852 Clement within 11 days in 2022 with no conditions beyond the standard 'Bona Fide Eating Place' requirement and compliance with Planning Code Section 202.2(a)(1) location and operating controls. Demonstrates routine approval pattern continues on this block.

comparables.why_comparable: Same address as above (852 Clement St), Type 41 ABC referral one year earlier, approved 2021.
comparables.key_takeaway: Prior Type 41 approval at 852 Clement in 2021 within 10 days, described as 'continuation of an existing use.' Shows Planning treats Type 41 licenses for restaurants in the Inner Clement NCD as permitted uses requiring only ABC and health department coordination, not discretionary review.

comparables.why_comparable: 100 meters away at 800 Clement St, Type 41 ABC referral for non-formula restaurant, approved 2022 in the Inner Clement NCD.
comparables.key_takeaway: Type 41 approved within 14 days at 800 Clement in 2022 with no conditions. Planning's description emphasized 'non-formula retail restaurant use,' confirming that independent restaurants with beer-and-wine are principally permitted and processed as routine agency referrals in this district.

comparables.why_comparable: 57 meters away at 832 Clement St, limited restaurant (DPH referral), approved 2021 in the Inner Clement NCD.
comparables.key_takeaway: Limited restaurant at 832 Clement approved within 35 days in 2021 as a DPH referral with no Planning conditions. Confirms that even new food-service establishments without prior use history are approved quickly in this corridor when zoning-compliant.

comparables.why_comparable: 235 meters away at 4724 Geary Blvd, Type 41 ABC referral for restaurant in the adjacent Geary Boulevard NCD, approved 2023.
comparables.key_takeaway: Type 41 approved in 2023 within 98 days (longer than Inner Clement cases) at Geary Boulevard with standard 'Bona Fide Eating Place' and Section 202.2(a) controls. Slightly longer timeline may reflect workload variation, but no additional neighborhood-specific restrictions despite Geary's similar density.

comparables.why_comparable: 208 meters away at 315 8th Ave, conditional use authorization for restaurant expansion with existing Type 41 license, filed 2020 and withdrawn 2022 in the Inner Clement NCD. This is a use decision record, not an agency referral.
comparables.key_takeaway: The only discretionary use decision within 1,000 feet in the last decade was a CUA for a restaurant expansion (merging two tenant spaces). The applicant withdrew after two years; the record does not state why, but the fact that a straightforward beer-and-wine restaurant operating in one space avoids CUA review entirely highlights the difference between principally permitted and conditional uses.

comparables.why_comparable: 67 meters away at 939 Clement St, conditional use authorization to intensify restaurant use (add 24 seats on ground floor), approved 1990 in the Inner Clement NCD. This is a use decision record.
comparables.key_takeaway: This 1990 CUA approval for restaurant intensification (adding seats) predates the current Planning Code framework. Under today's Code Section 716, first-story restaurants with beer-and-wine are principally permitted and do not trigger CUA review, showing that the regulatory path has simplified for standard restaurant concepts.

comparables.why_comparable: 94 meters away at 823 Clement St, full restaurant (DPH referral) approved 2019 after 3-year closure for seismic upgrading, in the Inner Clement NCD.
comparables.key_takeaway: Full restaurant at 823 Clement approved within 29 days in 2019 despite three years of inactivity. Planning treated it as a continuation of a legal non-conforming use rather than a new establishment, showing flexibility for restaurants resuming operations after tenant improvements or closures.

comparables.why_comparable: 272 meters away at 4601 Geary Blvd, Type 41 ABC referral for restaurant in the Geary Boulevard NCD, approved 2021.
comparables.key_takeaway: Type 41 at Geary Boulevard approved within 19 days in 2021 with standard 'bonafide eating place' condition per Section 202.2. Geary Boulevard NCD has similar density to Inner Clement, and approvals follow the same expedited agency-referral pattern for beer-and-wine restaurants.

patterns.pattern: Type 41 ABC licenses for restaurants in the Inner Clement NCD are approved as routine agency referrals within 10–35 days with no Planning Commission hearing. Every Type 41 application within 500 feet since 2016 was approved, most within two weeks.

Planning imposes only one standard condition on Inner Clement Type 41 approvals: the operator must 'operate as a Bona Fide Eating Place' per Planning Code Section 202.2, meaning alcohol service is ancillary to meals. No site-specific operating conditions (hours, security, noise) appear in any recent approval.

ABC's undue-concentration flag does not delay or restrict Type 41 approvals in this corridor. Despite 11 active on-sale licenses within 500 feet and 27 within 1,000 feet, every restaurant Type 41 since 2016 was approved without additional Planning conditions related to concentration.

Conditional use authorization is not required for first-story beer-and-wine restaurants in the Inner Clement NCD. Only one CUA within 1,000 feet in the last decade involved a restaurant, and that was for a structural expansion merging two storefronts (withdrawn), not for the restaurant use itself.

DPH referrals for limited restaurants (no alcohol) are approved even faster than Type 41 referrals, typically within 7–35 days, with no Planning conditions. This baseline shows that the addition of beer-and-wine does not materially slow the process.

Adjacent Geary Boulevard NCD shows the same approval pattern for Type 41 restaurants but with slightly longer timelines (19–98 days), likely due to higher application volume district-wide rather than neighborhood opposition or scrutiny.

Restaurants resuming operations after closures or tenant improvements are treated as continuations of existing use rather than new establishments, shortening Planning review timelines and avoiding discretionary review even after multi-year gaps.

approval_signals: First-story location in the Inner Clement NCD (restaurant use is principally permitted by Planning Code Section 716)
Type 41 (beer-and-wine only) rather than Type 47/48 (full bar), which avoids conditional-use review
Non-formula retail concept (no chain affiliation stated)
Closing before midnight (standard restaurant hours align with NCD permitted-use expectations)
Immediate adjacency to two other active Type 41 licenses (908 and 914 Clement) approved in recent years
Continuous restaurant use history at 910 Clement dating to at least 2005, with prior ABC licenses on record
denial_signals: ABC's undue-concentration flag is triggered for this census tract, which may add 1–3 months to the ABC timeline and require a Public Convenience or Necessity letter from the city (not a Planning denial, but a state-level delay)
High saturation (27 on-sale licenses within 1,000 feet) has not led to Planning denials but could invite ABC protests from existing licensees or community groups during the 30-day posting period

expected_conditions.condition: The operator must operate as a bona fide eating place, meaning alcohol service is ancillary to meals, per Planning Code Section 202.2.
expected_conditions.basis: Every Type 41 approval within 500 feet since 2016 imposed this standard condition. The Planning Department's ABC referral approvals at 906 Clement (2016), 852 Clement (2021, 2022) and 800 Clement (2022) all stated 'Must operate as a Bona Fide Eating Place.'

expected_conditions.condition: The business is subject to the location and operating conditions of Planning Code Section 202.2(a)(1), which limits alcohol service hours and sets good-neighbor requirements.
expected_conditions.basis: The 2022 Type 41 approval at 852 Clement stated 'Subject to the location and operating conditions outlined in 202.2(a)(1).' Section 202.2(a)(1) requires compliance with use-specific controls in the zoning district and standard alcohol operating conditions.

expected_conditions.condition: ABC Type 41 licence limits service to beer and wine only; no distilled spirits may be served.
expected_conditions.basis: ABC Type 41 is defined as on-sale beer and wine for an eating place. The permit catalog entry states minors are allowed and the business must be a bona fide eating place.

expected_conditions.condition: The business must subscribe to organics (green bin) collection and, above size thresholds, participate in edible food recovery under SB 1383.
expected_conditions.basis: California law requires every commercial food generator to subscribe to organics collection. Cities enforce it through the business licence or health inspection; set up hauler service before opening.

filing_playbook.action: Confirm the missing inputs with the applicant and Planning before filing or paying any fees.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: The rules set the zoning, alcohol and building rows to insufficient information because the description does not give whether the business is part of a chain, the square footage, how the liquor licence will be obtained, what the space was last used as, the occupant load, or the existing occupancy group. Confirm those answers in writing with the applicant, then submit them to Planning's information desk or the Permit Center to settle the zoning and building answers before filing. If the space is under 2,500 square feet, not a formula retail chain, and was last used as a restaurant or food service, the use is principally permitted and no conditional use authorization is needed. If any answer triggers a conditional use (formula retail or over 2,500 square feet), file a pre-application meeting request with Planning before signing the lease or paying application fees.

filing_playbook.action: Form the legal entity with the California Secretary of State and obtain an EIN from the IRS.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: File LLC Articles of Organization (LLC-1) or corporation articles with the California Secretary of State online; the fee is $70 for an LLC or $100 for a corporation. File the Statement of Information within 90 days ($20 for an LLC, due every two years). Then apply for an Employer Identification Number (EIN) from the IRS online; it is issued immediately and free. The EIN and entity name are needed for every other permit, the bank account, the lease and the liquor licence.

filing_playbook.action: Register for a California seller's permit with CDTFA and a San Francisco business registration certificate with the Treasurer & Tax Collector.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Register online with the California Department of Tax and Fee Administration (CDTFA) for a seller's permit; it is free and often issued the same day. ABC will not issue a liquor licence until the seller's permit exists, so do this early. Then register the business with the San Francisco Treasurer & Tax Collector within 30 days of starting business in the city; the fee is tiered by gross receipts (e.g. $55 up to $100k, $625 at $1–1.5M for 2026–27). Every other city department asks for the Business Account Number (BAN), so register immediately after forming the entity.

filing_playbook.action: File a fictitious business name (DBA) statement with the County Clerk if the public-facing name differs from the legal entity name.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: File the FBN statement with the San Francisco County Clerk in person (photo ID) or by mail, then publish in a court-approved newspaper once a week for four weeks and file proof of publication within 45 days. The total cost is about $60–120. Banks and ABC want the filed statement. If the restaurant name matches the legal entity name exactly, skip this step.

filing_playbook.action: Submit DPH plan check for the kitchen build-out at the same time as the building permit application to DBI.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Any new food facility or remodel affecting the kitchen needs DPH approval of plans, finishes, equipment and menu. Submit two sets of scaled drawings, interior/exterior photos and a menu through the DPH portal; the 2026–27 flat fee is $2,207 for a new restaurant (8 hours), with extra review at $276/hr. DBI will route the building permit application to DPH for plan check; coordinate with your architect to submit both applications at the same time. After approval, schedule a pre-final inspection at ~80% complete and a final inspection, booking each with your plan reviewer at least two weeks ahead.

filing_playbook.action: File the building permit application with DBI for tenant improvements, including kitchen build-out, hood, grease interceptor, plumbing, electrical and ADA upgrades.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Submit stamped architectural plans with a complete scope of work (kitchen, hood, grease interceptor, restrooms, ADA upgrades) to DBI. Fees are a percentage of construction valuation, typically $800–15,000. The application is routed to Planning for zoning review (Section 175), DPH for health plan check, SFPUC for grease interceptor review, and SFFD for hood suppression system review. Separate electrical, plumbing and mechanical permits are pulled by licensed subcontractors. Hire an architect who has done San Francisco restaurants; incomplete plan sets bounce between departments and add months. Do not start construction before the permit is issued.

filing_playbook.action: Install a grease interceptor and submit the Installation Verification Form to SFPUC under the Fats, Oils & Grease (FOG) program.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Under the FOG Control Ordinance every food service establishment that cooks must install grease-capturing equipment; SFPUC inspectors assign a Discharger Category (1–3) that dictates the device type, and new restaurants must install it before opening. Submitting the Installation Verification Form earns a 14.2% reduction on the sewer portion of your bill. An undersized or missing interceptor is a common reason DBI withholds final sign-off. Coordinate with your plumber and the building permit review.

filing_playbook.action: Schedule Fire Department inspections for the commercial kitchen hood and place of assembly (if occupant load is 50 or more).
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Commercial cooking hoods need a suppression-system plan review and inspection routed with the building permit. If the occupant load is 50 or more, obtain a Place of Assembly permit from the SFFD Bureau of Fire Prevention ($446, 49 South Van Ness Suite 560) and a posted occupancy sign. The Entertainment Commission also requires this permit for venues of 50+. Schedule the final fire inspection before the DPH pre-opening inspection, typically two weeks ahead.

filing_playbook.action: Apply for the ABC Type 41 licence after DPH plan check is approved and the building permit is issued.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: File the Type 41 application online with ABC, attaching the signed lease, seller's permit, zoning sign-off from Planning (the ABC referral approval), and the entity documents. The initial fee is about $1,000–1,600. Post the public notice at the premises for 30 days. ABC sends the application to the Police Department and Planning Department for review; expect 60–120 days if unprotested. If the census tract is over its authorised count and ABC flags undue concentration, start the Public Convenience or Necessity (PCN) letter request from Planning at the same time you apply to ABC; recent approvals in this corridor show no PCN delays, but confirm with ABC's district office or Planning's ABC liaison before filing.

filing_playbook.action: Apply for the health permit to operate at least one month before opening, after DPH plan check is approved and one certified food safety manager is on staff.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Apply online with your BAN, Location ID (LIN) and federal tax ID; the $470 permit to operate application (2026–27) includes the initial inspection. The 2026–27 annual licence fee for restaurants and bars is $0 for 2026–28; reinspections are $276/hr. A change of ownership or entity type needs a new permit, and you cannot serve the public before it is issued. Walk the space against the DPH checklist a week before the inspection: missing hand sinks, unsealed surfaces or no hot water are the most common reasons for failed pre-opening inspections, which push openings by 2–3 weeks.

timeline_cost.notes: The time and cost shown are for the one approval the rules could decide: the health permit to operate. The health permit is issued 14–45 days after plan check and inspection, at a cost of $470–1,000 in government fees (2026–27 schedule). This is a time to approval, not to a denial or a withdrawal. The rules set the zoning, alcohol and building rows to insufficient information, so no timeline or cost is given for those approvals until the missing inputs are confirmed. Once the applicant confirms whether the business is a chain, the square footage, how the liquor licence will be obtained, what the space was last used as, the occupant load, and the existing occupancy group, the rules can decide whether a conditional use authorization, an ABC Type 41 licence investigation, or a building permit with change of occupancy applies. If the use is principally permitted (non-chain, under 2,500 square feet, first story) and the space was last used as a restaurant with no change of occupancy, expect the ABC Type 41 to take 60–120 days and the building permit 14–120 days, with combined government fees of roughly $3,000–18,000 depending on construction valuation. If a conditional use authorization is required (formula retail or over 2,500 square feet), add 120–300 days and $3,100–15,000 for the Planning Commission hearing.
